title: next 15.5.24 -> 15.5.27 (advisories GHSA-4jqv-mc3x-m676 and GHSA-mcj8-r9mp-w47p, medium) under the normal dependency policy, no exception: exact pin, lock regenerated and proven by the workflow (B-031; D-009-R017)
objective: The web-dependency-security check fails closed since the night of 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-08 (first seen on the integration run after pull request 467, a handoff document: run 37707415626, job 113084984518, step 'Blocking npm audit (--audit-level=low; dev deps included)', 2026-10-08 about 00:23 UTC; the other 20 jobs of that run succeeded, among them the website's build and its browser tests): `npm audit --audit-level=low` reports 'next 15.0.0 - 15.5.26', '1 moderate severity vulnerability', naming GHSA-4jqv-mc3x-m676 (CVE-2026-94543, 'Next.js has cache poisoning of SSG and ISR pages in self-hosted applications') and GHSA-mcj8-r9mp-w47p (CVE-2026-94484, 'Next.js has cache poisoning in SSG/ISR rendering that leads to cross-user content substitution and persistent denial of service'), each of severity medium (npm audit prints 'moderate'), each affecting next >= 15.0.0, < 15.5.27 (and >= 16.0.0, < 16.3.8), first patched in 15.5.27. The maintainer published them on 2026-09-30 at 16:14:22Z and 16:14:19Z (api.github.com/repos/vercel/next.js/security-advisories/<id>); they entered GitHub's advisory database on 2026-10-07 at 20:32:06Z and 20:31:13Z (api.github.com/advisories/<id>). The dependency check newly picked them up between 2026-10-07 22:53 UTC (the last run in which the same lock passed) and 2026-10-08 00:23 UTC. apps/web/package.json pins "next": "15.5.24" and apps/web/package-lock.json locks next, @next/env and eight @next/swc-* packages at 15.5.24. Repair it under the NORMAL dependency policy, with no exception of any kind: move the pin to exactly 15.5.27 and regenerate the lock through .github/workflows/generate-lockfile.yml (never by hand, never on a local machine). Registry facts read by the orchestrator on 2026-10-08 at 00:31 UTC from registry.npmjs.org: next 15.5.27 published 2026-09-30T16:19:50.862Z; @next/env 15.5.27 published 2026-09-30T16:08:30.736Z; the eight @next/swc-* platform packages at 15.5.27 published 2026-09-30 between 16:04:32Z and 16:06:50Z; every one more than 604800 seconds old at that reading (the youngest, next itself, 634307 s). Compared with 15.5.24, next 15.5.27 changes only the versions of @next/env and of the eight @next/swc-* packages it names (15.5.24 -> 15.5.27) and the range of its optional dependency sharp ('^0.34.3 || ^0.35.3' -> '^0.34.3 || ^0.35.4'), which the locked sharp 0.35.5 (an exact override) already meets; its peer dependencies and its engines entry are unchanged. No package name is new to the lock. GitHub's advisory database lists no advisory for next 15.5.27 at that reading. The machine gates decide: the workflow's npm audit must report zero findings at every severity and its committed-lock age gate must pass on every package; if either fails, STOP and report - no waiver, no exclusion, no change to .npmrc or to the gate.
business_reason: CLAUDE.md principle 15 and the dependency-security directive D-009: no dependency may carry an unresolved advisory affecting the installed version, and audits fail closed (D-009-R002); the web lock is regenerated through the CI workflow and validated there (D-009-R017). Blocker B-031: while the advisories stand, every new run fails the web-dependency-security check, and nothing merges on a run that predates them. The reviewed corrections that wait on this branch (pull request 466) passed their checks at 22:37 UTC, before the check began to report the advisories; they do not merge on that run. Ordinary work under the standing policy (ADR-006 Tier A; the dependency change itself is security-reviewed, gate G5); the fixed version already meets the 7-day rule, so no owner exception is needed or sought. The repair is contracted on the branch of pull request 466 because one ledger-touching branch is open at a time (every ledger command rewrites project-control/state.json); it changes none of that branch's reviewed files and depends on none of them.
